findings.description: The sentence added here ("A finding that holds the change while its own action asks for nothing is not something a response addresses, so it escalates at the round it appeared in rather than being waited on") is false whenever such a finding arrives alongside a patchable one. Concrete input: a round returning [{warning, no-op}, {error, auto-fix}]. internal/dialogue/dialogue.go:12 gives NeedingAPerson empty, Verdict escalated, Answerable = [the error/auto-fix one], round 1 < Cap, so After returns awaiting-response - the round parks, it does not escalate. dialogue.Responses.Unanswered (internal/dialogue/responses.go:80) only walks Answerable, so the warning/no-op is never waited on; the author answers the auto-fix one, `scrat continue` proceeds, and if round two is clean the run ends clean. report.FindingsOf (internal/report/report.go:74) reads only the latest round's document, so the round-one blocking finding is absent from the final verdict entirely. The exhaustive oracle in internal/dialogue/dialogue_test.go:98-109 encodes the parking behaviour, so the test suite and this sentence disagree about the same input.

The new park-anyway path leaves the run reachable for reading only; the next command kills it. Trace: removeWorktree fails, park saves the run as awaiting-response with run.Worktree still pointing at the surviving directory, liftTheSeal makes it writable again. The author responds, then `scrat continue` reaches internal/reviewer/advance.go:75, where taken.Checkout hits internal/snapshot/snapshot.go:141-149: the path exists, so `git worktree add` refuses and, because presentAlready is true, the directory is deliberately not removed. Checkout returns an error and advance.go:77 calls fail(), ending the run as `failed`. Nothing on the continue path attempts the teardown that was skipped, so the completed review still cannot be advanced by any command - the dead end is deferred one step and now carries a `failed` verdict. The parked status also says nothing about it: the leftover is recorded only as a runlog field, so the author's first sight of the problem is the failed run.

A new normative requirement ("A failure to tear it down SHALL NOT stop the run being published as parked, and SHALL be recorded against the round") is added with no scenario, and nothing in the repository exercises it. internal/reviewer has no test files at all; the only related coverage is the e2e scenario "A parked run has nothing left to tear down" (internal/e2e/dialogue_test.go:75), which is the success path, and no test asserts the round-parked event or its new "worktree" field. Because the requirement carries no scenario, `make scenario-coverage` (scripts/scenario-coverage) cannot notice the gap, and tasks.md was not extended either. The change's headline behaviour - a completed review is no longer discarded by a teardown failure - is therefore asserted only in prose; no test fails without the fix.

Appending before reading fixes the lost-claim problem, but the read is now downstream of a durable side effect and its failure is reported as if nothing was stored. If responses.jsonl cannot be parsed - a torn final line from a short write or a crash mid-append, or a line carrying a field this binary does not know, since dialogue.Parse uses DisallowUnknownFields and validates every line - then appendResponse has already succeeded and r.Responses() fails. RecordResponse returns a zero Responses and the error, so reviewer.Respond (internal/reviewer/respond.go:33-36) returns before recording the response-recorded runlog event and the CLI reports a failure. The author's claim is on disk, unacknowledged and unlogged, and each retry appends another duplicate line while still reporting failure. Before this change the read came first, so a document that could not be read meant nothing was written.

Both new Answers assertions are vacuous: held() builds a dialogue.Responses literal holding two responses to f1 and the test then asserts Answers("f1") == 2 (and at line 15, one literal response asserted as 1). That checks the fixture, not any recording behaviour, and it cannot fail unless Answers stops counting. The behaviour the scenario "Changing a response" names - that responding again reads as a replacement - now lives in runstore.Round.RecordResponse (internal/runstore/round.go:136), and no Go test asserts that boolean: internal/runstore/responses_test.go:58-69 and internal/report/parked_test.go:121 both discard it. Its only remaining evidence is the word "replaced" in the CLI output at internal/e2e/dialogue_test.go:729 and internal/e2e/testdata/script/dialogue.txtar:84. Either assert the replacement through RecordResponse or drop the tautologies, since For/Latest/Unanswered in the same subtest already carry the real claims.

With SaveResponses deleted, Responses.Encode has no production caller left; its only remaining use is the encode-then-parse round trip at internal/dialogue/responses_test.go:38. It is the whole-document serialisation that the append-only requirement exists to forbid, so it now survives as an exported convenience whose only guarantee is tested against itself.

risk_rationale: The two behavioural changes (park despite teardown failure, append-before-read) move in the right direction and the concurrency and journey tests around them are stronger, but the teardown path is untested and its recovery is incomplete, one added design sentence contradicts the routing rule for a reachable input, and the read-back can now report a stored response as a failure.
